reply.text:
Let me check what your long runs actually look like first. I can't see any logged runs or a running program for you yet, so I'll answer in general terms.

Legs fading in the last mile usually means the long run is a bit longer or faster than your current fitness supports. Three things help most:

1. Run the long run slower than feels necessary. Most of it should be at a pace where you could talk in full sentences. Going out too fast is the most common reason the last mile falls apart.
2. Build the long run gradually, adding a small amount most weeks. Back off every third or fourth week so your legs can absorb the work.
3. Keep your weekly running consistent, because a steady base matters more than any single long run. Strength work for legs (squats, lunges, step-ups, calf raises) helps them hold up late in a run.

Fueling and sleep matter too. Showing up to a long run under-fed or short on sleep makes the end of it harder.

If you tell me your current weekly mileage and how many days you can run, I can have the app build you a plan around it.
